name: CycleWire, requests from markup
summary: The CycleWire app with its interactions declared in markup with cyclewire/request, the way htmx builds them: links and forms fetch HTML fragments from the server and swap them in (the results, the header's cart summary, the quick view, the newsletter message), and <cw-stream> messages in an answer update the other parts of the page. The core loads up front, and the request action's code with the page.

variant.differs: Every interaction is cyclewire/request in the page's markup instead of a hand-written action: links and forms fetch HTML fragments from the server and swap them in, <cw-stream> messages in an answer update the rest of the page, and only the quick view has a small action of its own, to open the dialog once the request has filled it. It shows what CycleWire costs, and how fast it is, used the way htmx is.

idioms.choice: The core loads as a module in <head>, with a modulepreload link, as the performance guide recommends.

cyclewire/request is registered once, as the action "request", and the page's forms and links run it with cw-action="request" and a cw-target: each asks the server for HTML and swaps it in, with no JavaScript of the app's own but the quick view's.
Vite bundles the page's script, and actions are registered as loader functions, so cyclewire/request, with the morph and message code it brings, and the quick view action are chunks of their own.

The server writes the entry's <script> and <link rel="modulepreload"> tags from Vite's manifest, and the modulepreload polyfill is turned off rather than imported, as the backend integration guide allows. Preloading an action's imports stays on.

Add to cart, the action most visitors use first, runs cyclewire/request, so the request action is preloaded with the page: the server writes <link rel="modulepreload"> for its chunk and the chunks it imports, from Vite's manifest. The quick view's action loads on intent, the default, and on touch screens also once the page is idle.

Links request their href and forms their action, so each works without JavaScript through a full page load. The server tells the request action's fetches (Sec-Fetch-Dest: empty) from navigations and answers them with only the part the interaction needs, with Vary: Sec-Fetch-Dest.

Search as you type sits on the search form, so the query goes with the category's hidden field: cw-on-input="request" with cw-debounce="200" (the scenario's 200 ms; the docs' example uses 150), next to cw-action="request" for a submit, which waits out the same debounce. Input runs in restart mode, so each key aborts the request before it. Only the results are swapped, never the input.

The result count, and after a category link the search form's fields and the category links, come in the same answer as <cw-stream> messages, the request action's counterpart to htmx's out-of-band swaps. The category links are morphed, so the link that was tapped keeps focus.
Add to cart swaps the new count and total into the header's cart summary (cw-target=".cart"), so the header needs no store and cyclewire/signals is not used.
The newsletter's answer goes into #newsletter-status. An invalid address is answered with 422, a form sent back with its errors, which the request action shows like any answer.
The quick view link has an empty cw-prefetch: the prefetch plugin fetches the link's own URL on intent, next to the action's code, and the request takes that response.

The quick view runs a small action of the app's own, which runs cyclewire/request and then opens the dialog with showModal(): markup cannot open a modal once the answer is in. The platform's way, an Invoker Command (command="show-modal"), would open it before the product arrives, and needs a button where the page has a link that works without JavaScript.
